newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank sees '97 growth at 6.17 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank sees '97 growth at 6.17 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank projected on Tuesday that the island's gross domestic product would grow 6.17 percent in 1997, up from an official forecast of 5.7 percent for 1996.

The central bank, in a year-end package of projections for the coming year, said that consumer prices could be expected to rise by 3.31 percent in 1997 and that wholesale prices should fall 0.23 percent, continuing their recent downward trend.
In trade, the central bank projected that Taiwan could expect 1997 exports to grow 8.39 percent, up from an official 1996 full-year forecast of 6.80 percent.
The island's imports were expected to grow 7.34 percent in 1997, up from 1996's forecast of 4.11 percent, the central bank said in an official statement.
Private investment was likely to rise 8.5 percent, it said.
The bank showed general optimism about Taiwan's economic outlook for 1997.
"The economy will gradually recover next year and demand for liquidity will increase," bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong told reporters at a year-end news conference after the statement was issued.
